fichas.title: Concert Halls — Acoustics
fichas.summary: Concert-hall acoustics depend on room size, volume and proportions, seating arrangement, materials, surfaces and finishes, as well as the sound characteristics and arrangement of instruments. Direct sound and early side reflections are important; reverberation must suit the music, since excessive reverberation reduces clarity and insufficient reverberation can make music sound dull. Adjustable stage reflectors, curtains and banners, and movable panels opening promenades or foyer areas into the hall allow acoustic conditions and effective volume to be varied. Hard surfaces favor longer reverberation, while occupied upholstered seats can help maintain more uniform reverberation as audience numbers change. The page includes a graph relating reverberation, hall volume and music type, and a table of sound-absorption coefficients for surfaces by frequency.
